Laura/Jordan — adding a few specifics from the security side to make the intake efficient.

Redaction and artifact guidance (practical rules):
- PII: redact direct identifiers (SSN, full DOB, customer SSNs) from screenshots and sample exports. Replace with tokenized placeholders (e.g., <REDACTED_CUSTOMER_ID>).
- Secrets/keys: do not provide private keys, API secrets, or HSM materials. Provide key rotation logs, KMS policy screenshots, and an attestation PDF instead.
- Telemetry/logs: provide sampled time windows (5–10 minute extracts) and aggregated metrics. Where audit logs are sensitive, we will generate a hashed event id column so you can confirm integrity without exposing raw identifiers.
- Configuration dumps: provide sanitized exports where credentials are removed; include screenshots of config panels for verification.

Artifacts we will prepare (examples):
- SOC2-TypeII-excerpt.pdf (control descriptions and auditor statement)
- iso_scope_statement.pdf (ISO 27001 scope and exclusion notes)
- redaction_guidelines.pdf (policy and checklist)
- sample_artifact_manifest.csv (artifact name, control mapped, redaction flags)

On logistics: if Oakridge requires a staged handoff, we can put artifacts in a read-only Google Drive folder with limited IP allowlist and 90-day expiry. For particularly sensitive artifacts we can schedule a secure, monotonic transfer via SFTP with a temporary account.

I will start populating the sample_artifact_manifest.csv today and will attach the first artifact pack by EOD Tuesday (2026-10-13) per Jordan's timeline.

Kimberly Park
